nativeOutcome: One additional living-wage job placement attributable to the Center within the reporting year
decision: Do not publish a dollars-per-10-QALYs price. The Center has not defined the wage threshold, measured retention or earnings, identified a causal placement effect, or collected preference-based health utility. Employment is not itself a health state, and the nearest cost-utility literature evaluates specific supported-employment interventions in populations with diagnosed health conditions; it does not supply a transferable QALY coefficient per placement for this program or population.

candidateEvidence.nearestEvidence: Economic evaluations of supported employment or Individual Placement and Support for people with mental-health conditions
candidateEvidence.boundary: Some supported-employment studies measure QALYs directly, but their participants, intervention fidelity, comparators, health conditions, follow-up, and utility instruments differ from the Center's broad employment services. Their QALY results cannot be divided by job counts and transferred as a per-placement weight.

failedGates.label: Define and retain the employment outcome
failedGates.why: The published 30+ count does not define the living-wage threshold, job hours, benefits, start date, retention, earnings, duplicate people, or the reporting pathway that preceded each placement.

failedGates.label: Measure the Center's causal placement effect
failedGates.why: The Center reports placements without a concurrent comparison or baseline placement rate. The model's 25% attribution share is a decision scenario, not an evidence estimate, and a null remains plausible.

failedGates.label: Identify incremental employment-program cost
failedGates.why: The numerator is the entire audited Economic Development allocation, which also includes financial, housing, and small-business services. It is not an employment-program budget or a marginal funding quote.

failedGates.label: Establish a causal employment-to-health pathway
failedGates.why: Employment, income, job quality, discrimination, baseline health, and health utility are jointly determined. The Center did not measure whether any additional placement changed health rather than only employment status.

failedGates.label: Measure preference-based health utility
failedGates.why: No EQ-5D, HUI, SF-6D, AQoL, or other preference-based utility measure was collected. Quality-of-life findings from supported-employment studies do not create a utility coefficient for this population.

failedGates.label: Establish timing and persistence
failedGates.why: The published placement count has no 6- or 12-month retention, earnings trajectory, health-utility time points, onset, area under the curve, or post-program persistence.

failedGates.label: Reconcile public funding and marginal capacity
failedGates.why: Government grants supplied 55% of FY2024 revenue, individualized coaching enrollment is paused, and no dated marginal plan shows that a new private gift adds service capacity rather than replacing public or restricted funding.

illustrativeCounterfactual.arithmetic: $171,768 / [missing QALYs per additional retained placement] x 10 QALYs
illustrativeCounterfactual.publicationBoundary: No arithmetic result is shown because choosing a QALY weight would fabricate the central input. The native conditional placement scenario remains visible only as an audit trail; it is not a comparison price, rank, or recommendation.

requiredEvidence: Pre-specify the living-wage threshold, eligible cohort, service pathway, employment start, hours, benefits, and 6- and 12-month retention and earnings outcomes.
Use a randomized, phased, or credible matched comparison with complete participant flow, exposure, missing-data analysis, and a pre-specified causal estimand.
Collect preference-based utility at baseline and repeated follow-up for the same participants; estimate utility jointly with employment rather than importing a literature coefficient.
Publish the employment-program budget, active-component costs, public and restricted funding, displacement rule, capacity, and dated $100K, $1M, and $10M marginal plans.
